test_title: PYST 59: SSC CGL 2024 - General Knowledge (Held On 13 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A small object is placed on the focus on the left side of a convex lens. Where will the image be formed?

options.text: At the centre on the right side of the lens.
At infinity on the left side of the lens.
At infinity on the right side of the lens.
At the focus on the right side of the lens.

solution:
The correct answer is __**At infinity on the right side of the lens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed at the focus of a convex lens, the rays after refraction through the lens become parallel to each other.
 
• Parallel rays are considered to meet at infinity on the other side of the lens.
 
• Thus, the image formed will be at infinity on the right side of the lens.
 
• This image will be highly enlarged and real.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Lens:**

 
 
• A convex lens is thicker at the center than at the edges and is also known as a converging lens because it converges light rays that are initially parallel.
 
• It is used in various optical devices such as magnifying glasses, cameras, and corrective lenses for farsightedness.
 
 
 
• **Focus:**
 
 
• The focus (or focal point) of a lens is the point where parallel light rays converge (for a convex lens) or appear to diverge from (for a concave lens).
 
• The distance from the lens to the focus is called the focal length.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation by Convex Lens:**
 
 
• When an object is placed at the focus of a convex lens, the refracted rays become parallel, indicating that the image is formed at infinity.
 
• When the object is placed between the lens and the focus, the image formed is virtual, erect, and enlarged.
